solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: The top military players?

definitions.meaning: senior officers collectively are called the top ...
the trumpets, trombones and horns of an orchestra form its ... section

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idiomatic: generals are the military's top tier, and an orchestra's horn section shares the metal's name.

clue.text: Special balti Pam's used for dip

indicators.note: special suggests something made in an unusual way, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Pam's special curry served with a dipping sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dip' is immersion in baptism, not a sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Christening can involve immersion in water, so a font is a vessel for that ceremonial dip.

clue.text: Hanging at murder scene staged

definitions.meaning: a hanging is a wall tapestry
in Hamlet, Polonius is stabbed hiding behind a tapestry, so it was at a murder in a staged play

explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry wall hanging is named after a French town, and Shakespeare's Polonius dies behind one.

clue.text: Long-distance travellers resort to fix that's incomplete

parts.note: a spa is a resort

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to cement is to fix firmly

explanation.surface: Far-travelling tourists heading for a resort to finish an unfinished repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's incomplete' drops the T of CEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronauts journey vast distances off Earth, making them the ultimate long-haul travellers.

clue.text: Weaver to drink a toast

parts.note: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A weaver about to raise a glass to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaver' looks like a trade but names Shakespeare's Bottom, the weaver given an ass's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cheery invitation to drain glasses, used as a drinking salute.

clue.text: Army officer cut down, causing stir in navy

indicators.note: cut down means the word is shortened at its end

parts.note: a brigadier is a senior army officer

explanation.surface: An army officer felled, causing a commotion at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stir' is slang for prison: a ship's jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval prison or lock-up on a warship is the sailors' version of jail, and stir is slang for jail.

clue.text: Lines in praise of some satellite TV sport?

parts.note: an ode is addressed to its subject, so to signals praise
a means some, one
Sky is the UK satellite television broadcaster
a lark is a bit of sport or fun

explanation.surface: Poetry celebrating a satellite channel's sports coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelley's ode title read as 'to a Sky lark'. Sky is a British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's famous poem is a set of verse lines addressed in praise of a bird.

clue.text: City of old to which a measure of power returns

indicators.note: returns means the words are read back the other way

parts.note: the watt is the unit of power

explanation.surface: An ancient city to which a degree of power returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns A WATT into TTAWA, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's capital is an example of a city.

clue.text: Conflict the Sun stayed out of

definitions.text: Conflict the Sun stayed out of

parts.words: Conflict the Sun stayed out of
parts.note: Sun is Sunday: a week with Sunday left out has six days, and the 1967 Arab-Israeli war lasted that long

explanation.walkthrough: 'the Sun' reads as a newspaper or star but is Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1967 Arab-Israeli conflict lasted just under a week, hence its name.

clue.text: Did long wooden drawer that only opens

parts.note: pine furniture is wooden

indicators.note: only opens means only the first letter of drawer is used

explanation.surface: A wooden drawer that only slides open is a long-time wish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' seems to be furniture but gives only its opening letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearned is a synonym: to long for something is to yearn or ache for it.

clue.text: A head's power dissolved at a price

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: dissolved means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's authority melting away at a cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissolved' rearranges AT A PRICE into ERCAPITA, which follows P.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means for each person, as in a cost quoted at so much a head.

clue.text: Flipping idiot drinking neat poison

indicators.note: drinking means the outer piece takes in the inner one
flipping turns the word over, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a nit is a fool
neat is an old word for cattle; an ox is one

explanation.surface: A cursing complaint about a fool knocking back undiluted poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse but signals the reversal, and 'drinking' the container. 'neat' is the old word for cattle, not undiluted.
explanation.definitionFit: A toxin is a poisonous substance, especially one produced by a living organism.

clue.text: One note rung, displaying harmony

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a rung of a ladder is a step

explanation.surface: A single bell note sounded, showing musical harmony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rung' looks like a bell's past tense but is a ladder's rung.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching or acting in step means being in agreement, in harmony with others.

clue.text: Spotted gardens nestling in southern plain

indicators.note: nestling in means one piece sits snugly inside the other

parts.note: plain and bald both mean unadorned
Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in west London

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a garden tucked into a southern plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nestling in' places the gardens between the two halves; Kew is London's Royal Botanic Gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a horse with irregular patches of white and another colour, so patchy or spotted.

clue.text: Offensive President, out on a limb, to be contained

indicators.note: to be contained means the rearranged letters go inside the first piece

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US president

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A rude president, isolated, must be kept in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out on a limb' looks like an idiom for isolated; 'out' is the anagram signal and 'to be contained' the container. Abe is Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: Something loathsome or detestable is offensive in the strongest sense.

clue.text: Maiden invited round for social event

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
invited means asked
a ball is round, a sphere

explanation.surface: A young woman asked out for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is a sphere here, not 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance where guests wear masks is a kind of formal party.

clue.text: Mob I clash with turns in disarray

indicators.note: turns means the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A crowd and I fighting in turns, all chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang word means chaotically disorganised, a muddle.

clue.text: Some follow assailant, backing off

indicators.note: backing means the run of letters is read in reverse
some means only part of the words follow assailant is used

explanation.surface: Advice to chase an attacker, then retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes LOWA from 'folLOW Assailant'; 'backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Absent without leave describes a soldier who has gone off without permission.

clue.text: Gamble rent's on time and put away in box?

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the next piece follows

parts.note: to lay a bet is to gamble
rent is the past of rend, i.e. tore, and 's gives S

explanation.surface: A gamble about rent and storing something in a box on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is a coffin, not a crate.
explanation.definitionFit: Burying someone in a coffin is a euphemism of putting them in their final resting place.

clue.text: Vessel that's not long transporting PM

indicators.note: transporting means carrying the second piece within

parts.note: soon means after not long
Pitt the Elder and Pitt the Younger were British prime ministers

explanation.surface: A ship that briefly carries the prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a receptacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle for spit is a vessel, here a container rather than a boat.

clue.text: On return, trains to become make-up artist?

indicators.note: on return means the word is read back the other way

parts.note: rail is the general word for trains as transport

explanation.surface: Someone trains, on returning, to work in theatrical cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up artist' is not a cosmetics expert but someone who makes things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fibber is cryptically someone who makes up stories, a fabricator of falsehoods.

clue.text: Mean surrounding chap with lasso, possibly without justification

indicators.note: surrounding means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to mean something is to imply it
a roper is a cowboy who ropes cattle, one example of a man with a lasso

explanation.surface: A rough cowboy wielding a lasso, perhaps unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' is the container; 'possibly' marks the lasso-wielder as one example of such a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting wrongly or unfittingly means doing it with no proper warrant or justification.

clue.text: Greek article containing nothing about Russian composer

indicators.note: containing means the first pieces hold the second
about means the word turns round

parts.note: nil means nothing
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Greek piece of writing featuring nothing on a Russian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the reversal and 'containing' the container; 'article' is the grammatical a, not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka is regarded as the father of Russian classical music.

clue.text: Man's ending in jail, but strangely very happy

indicators.note: in means the letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
strangely means the letters are oddly rearranged
ending means the final letter of the word Man

explanation.surface: A man finishing up in prison, yet oddly delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges JAIL BUT into JUBILAT, and 'in' puts N, the end of 'Man', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Exultant joy is a strong form of happiness, so a synonym for delighted.

clue.text: Fellow patient one keeps lifting roughly

indicators.note: keeps means the outer piece holds the inner

parts.note: Job is the biblical figure famed for patience

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue means the letters go upwards, reversed

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly

explanation.surface: A tolerant man who keeps raising things carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' reverses upwards in a down clue and 'keeps' is the container; 'patient one' is the biblical figure, not a hospital patient.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's given name stands for a man, a fellow.

clue.text: Wall decoration fastened, but not entirely firm

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: stuck means fastened
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A wall ornament fixed up, though not quite solidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims STUCK to STUC; 'firm' is a company here, not solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine plaster used for moulded ornament and coating on walls is a type of decoration.

clue.text: Swindle is issue for uncle to mention

indicators.note: to mention is to say aloud, so the word is heard

parts.note: an uncle's child, his issue, is a nephew's or niece's cousin

explanation.surface: A con involving an uncle's offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, not a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to cheat or trick someone, so to swindle.

clue.text: Books containing note found in skip

indicators.note: containing means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Books with a note discovered in a rubbish skip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skip' is a verb, to leave out, not a waste container.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out or pass over it is to skip it.

clue.text: See that fleece covers part of body

indicators.note: covers means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to fleece is to swindle, to con
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Seeing that a sheep's coat covers part of an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' means cheat, not wool.
explanation.definitionFit: The large intestine's main section is an organ, an anatomical part.

clue.text: For dictator, perhaps, canes will do

indicators.note: a dictator is one who dictates, speaking words out for another to take down

parts.note: bamboos are canes, and will contracts to 'll

explanation.surface: A tyrant might find caning does the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' is not a tyrant but someone dictating: 'bamboos'll' is spoken and heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating or tricking them, i.e. to hoodwink.

clue.text: However short, tea break is capital!

indicators.note: short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: but means however
cha is a colloquial word for tea
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: An exclamation that even a brief tea break is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' looks like British slang for 'excellent' but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania's seat of government is this city, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: A piece that's just gross?

parts.note: a gross figure has no deductions, so it is the answer; read as one word it is a musical work for nine players

explanation.walkthrough: Gross and net are opposite money terms: a gross amount carries 'no net'.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition for nine instruments or voices is a musical piece.
